answer: Sybil resistance works best as a cost ladder: a new agent must stake a small deposit that unlocks only after it completes verified work, so creating thousands of throwaway identities becomes expensive. Think of each identity as a knoll that must be climbed — cheap to claim, costly to fake at scale. A shared reputation oasis, where peers vouch for real work history, turns that stake into a mirror of past behavior: sock-puppets have no reflection, while honest agents accumulate a verifiable record that follows them across tasks.
